relevance_note: The paper describes a three-generation family carrying a TNFAIP3 nonsense variant: 'Here we describe a family with HA20 caused by a novel TNFAIP3 loss-of-function mutation'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown manually; the paper has no patient tables. JSON was assembled by a short Python script in the scratch directory from values I chose by reading; spans were checked by script for verbatim occurrence. Individuals are labelled with the pedigree labels (I-2, II-1, II-4, III-1); Figures 4 and 5 also call II-1 'patients 1' and III-1 'patient 2'. Non-carrier relatives shown in the pedigree are not described and get no rows. I-2 is described only as an 'obligate carrier' (no direct genotyping reported); she has a variant row but zygosity is left 'not reported'. Zygosity 'heterozygous' for II-1, II-4 and III-1 rests on the family-level statement 'a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) loss-of-function mutation'. Inheritance is left 'not reported' for everyone: the paper says I-2 (mother of the index) is an obligate carrier and III-1 is the index's daughter, but it never states from whom any carrier inherited the variant. The variant is printed in non-standard notation 'c.A271T: p.(Lys91*)' with Ensembl IDs 'ENSG00000118503:ENST00000433680' (no version); recorded as printed, no transcript added. III-1's age_at_diagnosis ('at the age of 4 years') is the age at diagnosis of polyarticular JIA, not of HA20; the ages 30 years (II-1) and 8 years (III-1) are from the Figure 4/5 legends (age at PBMC sampling) and recorded as age at last evaluation. Autoimmune thyroiditis was 'diagnosed ... at an early age' in all four carriers; recorded in severity_or_detail, not as a numeric age. Checklist calls: 'articular symptoms' (II-1) counted as observed for 'arthritis or arthralgia'; 'atrophic gastritis' as observed for 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; psoriasis as observed for 'skin lesions'; 'repeated genital HSV infections' as observed for 'recurrent infections'. Anaemia (II-1) left 'not reported' for 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' because no autoimmune cause is stated; I-2's liver failure left 'not reported' for 'autoimmune hepatitis'; the lung reaction is not called interstitial lung disease, so ILD is 'not reported'. Not recorded as phenotypes: ex vivo PBMC cytokine results (placed in functional_evidence_statement) and the plasma IL-18 increase in 'TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) carriers' (supplementary figure, carriers not named in the text). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null: the paper does not say any patient was reported before. Minor wording differences, not treated as contradictions: Figure 1 legend says 'severe autoinflammatory lung reaction' and lists 'genital papillomatosis', while the Results say 'severe inflammatory lung reaction' and omit papillomatosis. No contradictions found.

functional_evidence_statement.value: In transfected HEK cells the p.(Lys91*) mutant failed to inhibit TNF-α-induced NF-κB reporter activation, was expressed only as an N-terminal fragment, and had a severely impaired protein–protein interactome. Patient II-1 PBMCs showed elevated IL-1β and IL-18 secretion that caspase-8 inhibition suppressed, and active caspase-1 in monocytes after whole-blood inflammasome stimulation was increased in II-1.
span: The wt A20 dose-dependently inhibited TNF-α induced NF-κB pathway activation, whereas the p.(Lys91*) mutant failed to do so, clearly suggesting a haploinsufficiency (figure 2C).
the p.(Lys91*) mutant was detected only with an N-terminal tag (figure 2A), suggesting that only an N-terminal fragment is produced and no alternative start codons are used
We found elevated secretion of IL-1β and IL-18 in PBMCs of the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) carriers
levels of active caspase-1 in monocytes after whole blood inflammasome stimulation were increased only in patient II-1
caspase-8 inhibitor Z-IETD-FMK efficiently suppressed IL-1β and IL-18 secretion in PBMCs of the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*)-positive patients
